definitions.holds: The selected project statement is supported for its stated art/metadata scope by the sampled saved evidence. This does not imply immutable control, successful browser rendering, or exhaustive collection coverage.
definitions.onchain-data-offchain-pointer: Art/data bytes or creative code are evidenced on Ethereum, while ordinary tokenURI or a marketplace media/preview field points off-chain. This supports a data-storage claim and is not a false claim.
definitions.contradicted: Saved evidence establishes that the selected project statement is false as stated, accounting for alternate data paths and its scope. Only this outcome may be called a failed claim.
definitions.unverifiable: The scoped statement is not resolved by available reads, incomplete coverage, gas limits or ambiguous wording; neither true nor false is asserted.

claims.population: The 283 original reviewed candidate collections in data/claims/review_population.csv; directory-only and rejected candidates are not claimants.

examples.name: Moonbirds
examples.text: The pixelated art is fully on-chain (aka “in-chain”)—meaning that the images are rendered directly from the Ethereum smart contracts.
examples.reason: The website claim is scoped to pixelated art. The live renderer's legacyRenderer points to 0xb1befc9e7b76c1e846ebbf3e6e1ab029c86e7435; artworkPixels(1) and artworkURI(1,1) return pixels and an inline BMP directly. The full tokenURI(1) reverted inconclusively; the correctly addressed 15x legacy BMP read hit this provider's 50M gas cap. Illustration/animation URI control remains separate.

examples.name: Blitmap
examples.text: All data is completely on chain.
examples.reason: tokenDataOf(1) and tokenSvgDataOf(1) return bitmap data and SVG directly from Blitmap; tokenURI(1) still uses the HTTP API and its base URI remains settable.

examples.name: ChainFaces
examples.text: All attributes and metadata are on-chain and easily viewable via the etherscan UI.
examples.reason: getFace(1) and getGolfScore(1) return on-chain ASCII art and attributes; tokenURI(1) retains the Azure HTTP pointer. The data claim does not promise that HTTP endpoint will work.

examples.name: Chain Runners
examples.text: Chain Runners are Mega City renegades 100% stored and generated on chain.
examples.reason: The live routing contract's onChainTokenURI(1) returns inline SVG art from a separate on-chain renderer. The collection tokenURI(1) uses an HTTP API; mutable routing is a separate observation, not a false storage claim.

examples.name: Art Blocks (Curated contract; Fidenza, Ringers)
examples.text: Art Blocks tokens store their metadata fully on-chain, ensuring collectors that their NFTs will always remain accessible and immutable.
examples.reason: Fidenza projectScriptByIndex(78,0) and tokenIdToHash(78000000) confirm on-chain creative data. The selected documentation also claims complete metadata accessibility and immutability; this is broader than the checked script/hash sample. The HTTP pointer is not itself a contradiction.

examples.name: CryptoSkulls
examples.text: Every CryptoSkull is fully embedded on-chain. No external storage. No broken links. No missing files.
examples.reason: All 10,000 skull indices return attributes and 576 on-chain RGB pixels from CryptoSkullsData at 0x9a7b94954751d539c63e16aa6e0557c451251394. The collection tokenURI still uses IPFS; both data writes and the collection base URI remain owner-controlled.

examples.name: MoonCats
examples.text: The 25440 MoonCats rescued are acclimating to their life as [fully on-chain](https://mooncatrescue.com/about) collectible critters.
examples.reason: The original 2017 MoonCatRescue contract 0x60cd862c9c687a9de49aecdc3a99b74a4fc54ab6 returns the five-byte cat seed via rescueOrder and getCatDetails; the acclimator wrapper tokenURI uses HTTP and its setBaseURI remains owner-controlled. Reconstructing pixels also requires the published MoonCat parser; this check establishes seed storage.

funnel.definition: A live, effective URI-string setter, renderer/descriptor address swap, or upgrade on the ordinary token metadata/art path, controlled by one EOA or one multisig account. Data-only edits are excluded. A multisig account may require several signatures; this does not mean one private key.

lanes.class_label: Renderer held by one wallet key
lanes.summary: The core is owned by a Safe multisig. Its current renderer is held by one wallet key: owner-only setBaseUri(string) and setAnimationBaseUri(string) redirect illustrated-art and animation URLs. They do not rewrite the legacy on-chain pixel data; setArtwork(uint256,bool) and setArtworks(uint256[],bool[]) are token-holder controls.
An ordinary key owns the contract and set the renderer address 3 times in the saved history. An alternate on-chain renderer supplies SVG; the ordinary tokenURI points to HTTP.
An ordinary key owns the contract and set the renderer address 8 times between 2026-05 and 2026-09. Replacing the renderer or its storage source can change displayed pixels and metadata.
